Despite this, he continued to call them to the upright religion, and a few people followed him, while the disbelievers persisted in their transgression. So Allah withheld the rain from them, and Nuh called them to believe so that Allah would lift the punishment from them; they believed and Allah lifted the punishment, but they returned to their disbelief. He kept calling them for nine hundred and fifty years; then Allah commanded him to build the ark and to take with him a pair of every kind; then the flood came and drowned them all.

Ibrahim lived among a people who worshipped the stars, and that did not satisfy him; he sensed by his innate nature that there is a greater God, until Allah guided him and chose him for His message. Ibrahim began calling his people to the oneness of Allah and His worship, but they denied him and tried to burn him, and Allah saved him from their hands. Allah made the prophets from the progeny of Ibrahim: Isma‘il and Ishaq were born to him. Ibrahim built the Ka‘bah together with Isma‘il.

Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.

Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: the unlettered Arab prophet of Banu Hashim. He was born in Mecca a few months after his father Abdullah died. His mother Aminah died while he was still a child. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib cared for him, then his uncle Abu Talib. He tended sheep for a time. At twenty-five he married Lady Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. He called people to Islam, meaning belief in the one Allah and His Messenger. He began his call in Mecca; its people persecuted him, so he migrated to Medina, where a number of supporters gathered around him in 622 CE. That year became the start of the Hijri calendar. He possessed many praiseworthy qualities and was the seal of prophets and most honourable of messengers. Allah revealed to him the Noble Quran containing the teachings of Islam, which Allah approved as humanity's religion. Its monotheism and legislation made it a universal religion encompassing every aspect of life and suitable for all people at every time and place. His message, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was therefore for all people. Through its merits Islam spread throughout the earth. He died after performing the Farewell Pilgrimage.
